title: Inject ParentAnalyticsRepository into RestoreGuard instead of constructing it inline
rule: SM-7 (repositories/services/DAOs constructed only inside their @riverpod provider or a test override)
why: RestoreGuard._resolve() hand-constructs ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl(db) directly inside the navigation-check method rather than receiving it as an injected dependency — a literal SM-7 violation. ParentAnalyticsRepository has no Riverpod provider anywhere in the codebase (it's hand-constructed at 2 more sites outside this batch: local_data_upload_service.dart and device_restore_service.dart), so today nothing lets a test or a future caller swap this repository via ProviderScope; a test that wants to fake it has to fake the whole UserDatabase instead. Real-world cost is low today (the class is a thin, stateless DAO wrapper, and RestoreGuard's closure-based constructor is otherwise a deliberately Riverpod-free, easily-testable design — see its excellent test suite), but if SM-7 ships a checker this line (and its 2 siblings) will need either a wrapping provider or a documented exception.
recommendation: Either add a parentAnalyticsRepositoryProvider (@riverpod, takes UserDatabase) and inject it into RestoreGuard's constructor alongside getDatabase, or explicitly document ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl as an intentional non-Riverpod infra helper exempt from SM-7.
acceptance_criteria: Once SM-7 has a checker, ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl( outside core/analytics/ appears only inside a @riverpod provider body, or is allowlisted with a stated reason.
